direction: Original painted fresco assets; material, composition and measured registration, not a screen-space texture filter.
reference: User fresco FPS reference f2dbf55c; interpreted visually and through text briefs. Historical seals preserved separately.

entries.prompt:
Create one production-ready game texture atlas, square 2048x2048, exactly FOUR equally sized square material tiles in a precise 2 by 2 grid, with NO gaps, NO labels, NO frame or border around the atlas. Each quadrant fills exactly one quarter and is an orthographic flat material, absolutely no perspective and no cast shadow.

The entire atlas is original hand-painted medieval Italian buon fresco, inspired by Giovanni da Modena's Inferno and the pale fresco chapel in the supplied reference: colored pigment embedded in chalky plaster, quiet broad brush modelling, thin red-brown sinopia underdrawing, muted limited mineral pigments, warm ivory lime, yellow ochre, cinnabar, burnt umber and blue-black. It must retain the organic authority of a mural painting, NOT cel shading, not smooth vector art, not a photograph of bricks, not a glossy PBR material, not a pixelated or noisy texture. Fine small irregular lime wear and very few hairline cracks, never thick huge polygonal cracks. Controlled low contrast grain so objects remain readable in front.

TOP LEFT, exactly x0-50% y0-50%: light warm chalk plaster with large uneven rectangular ashlar courses subtly suggested by thin umber lines under the plaster. Most surface is warm old ivory, broad cloudy ochre brush washes. Large blocks, each with gentle painted volume. Calm usable game wall texture. Seamless repeat on all four edges of this tile.
TOP RIGHT, exactly x50-100% y0-50%: the same plaster as seen inside a shadowed chapel recess, muted blue-grey charcoal pigments with warm umber undertones, soft broad hand-painted modelling, few dark painted mortar lines. Darker than the first tile but not pure black. No literal window, object, symbol or scene. Seamless repeat.
BOTTOM LEFT, exactly x0-50% y50-100%: worn cinnabar red and burnt ochre painted plaster used on architectural bands and columns, warm earthy red ground with irregular broad old brush marks, a few faded pale marks, no lettering or defined iconography. A low contrast restrained field, no modern brick grid. Seamless repeat.
BOTTOM RIGHT, exactly x50-100% y50-100%: medieval painted terracotta and faded slate-grey flagstones in a regular orthogonal grid viewed directly from above, thin warm pale grout, subdued colors lighter and calmer than enemies. About 4 by 4 large rectangular slabs per tile; worn terracotta predominates, alternate some grey blue and warm pale stone, no checkerboard high contrast. Thin hand-drawn sinopia edges and very restrained tiny lime loss. Seamless repeat.

No characters, no weapons, no text, no HUD. The texture itself must carry the craftsmanship; it will be used on 3D surfaces without a posterization filter. Output just this exact 2x2 atlas.

Create one original panoramic background painting for a dark first person game, 3072x1024 wide, a continuous panorama with horizontally seamless left and right edges, NO frame and NO UI or lettering. It will be wrapped around the distant horizon as a cylindrical fresco.

Match the painted medium of Giovanni da Modena's Inferno, with compositional depth from the hell panel of Hieronymus Bosch, heroic small gestures reminiscent of Michelangelo's Last Judgement, restrained orderly passage of souls as in Memling. This is NOT a digital fantasy concept art painting. It is an actual matte early Italian fresco on aged lime: broad ochre and slate pigment washes, thin sinopia contours, handmade volume within silhouettes, restrained fine plaster grain and very few hairline marks, no large cracks, no bloom, no photorealism, no 3D rendering, no pixel dithering, no black cartoon outlines.

Composition precise for a game horizon:
Top 50 percent: somber desaturated blue-grey and warm ash sky, broad heavy smoke shapes, old lime ground visible, quiet and low contrast. No sun or moon or stars.
Middle 25 percent: layered distant medieval towers, bridges, rooflines and a vast gate in a burning damned city, disappearing into slate smoke. Rhythmic tongues of painted ochre and iron-red flame at staggered heights, not a uniform orange stripe. One distant huge shadow of a seated infernal figure is only half discernible in smoke toward the right quarter, never a front-and-centre enemy. The horror is scale and the impassive world watching, no spectacle fireworks.
Bottom 25 percent: dark umber and slate silhouettes of ruined walls, tiny procession of bowed adult human souls along a wall, clothed simply, barely visible and clearly distant, tiny frozen narrative gestures. Several depth layers from dark near silhouettes to faded slate far city. Darkest at bottom edge which should tile in color vertically to near black.

The design should make a player feel the visible test courtyard is a small threshold within an immense judgement. Ominous, solemn, deeply human, not a heroic poster. The drawing is subtle enough never to compete with nearby attack silhouettes. Output the panorama only.

Create a production game sprite atlas on a truly TRANSPARENT background, 2048x1024, exactly 4 columns and 2 rows of EIGHT equally sized square 512x512 cells, NO lines, no labels, no cell borders. Each sprite fully contained in its cell with minimum 48 pixel transparent gutters on every side; all objects have their contact base at 90% cell height. Camera frontal with slightly visible top surfaces. No background plane, no paper rectangle, no floor shadow.

Style: everything is original hand-painted Italian early Renaissance fresco pigment, like Giovanni da Modena's Inferno, pale warm ivory and blood-red sinopia outlines, yellow ochre, charcoal blue, burnt umber. Broad flat brush masses but believable volume painted within them, restrained fine chalk texture inside the silhouettes only. Eerie medieval liturgical objects, solemn horror. NOT modern fantasy game loot icons, NOT glossy 3D or chrome, NOT cute cartoon, NOT noisy pixel art or vector art. Matte iron painted in near-black blue with chalk highlights, no specular highlights.

Top row cells 1,2,3,4: four consecutive animated poses of the SAME low three-legged medieval iron brazier bowl, narrow dark wrought iron legs, umber bowl, flames painted as rhythmic pointed ochre and bone-white shapes with red-brown tips. The flame changes silhouette from left lean to upright to right lean to upright, but the identical bowl and legs stay perfectly registered at the same size and position in all four cells. Overall sprite height 75% of cell, width 50%. Flame occupies the upper third, no floating sparks beyond gutters.
Bottom row cell 1 (frame5): a tall emaciated, hooded stone mourning effigy on a small pedestal, bowed face obscured, folded hands and heavy ragged cloak, chalk-grey limestone painted with umber contours, horrifying through grief rather than spikes; occupies 78% height, 35% width.
Bottom row cell 2 (frame6): low heap of old adult skulls and rib bones, linen scraps, dark red cloth; large readable bone masses, 65% width and 35% height anchored at same floor baseline, no gore.
Bottom row cell 3 (frame7): three guttering beeswax altar candles of different heights on a low black iron plate, pale ochre wax, tiny painted flames, 65% height 50% width.
Bottom row cell 4 (frame8): a small sealed reliquary casket in dark wood and dull iron, a scrap of red burial cloth hanging down, an old cracked pale human death mask on top, 55% height 65% width. No symbols that resemble text.

No cross-cell overlap and no partial cut-off objects. Transparent empty cell space. Output only this game atlas.

Create a game sprite sheet of one animated resting shrine, 2048x1024 transparent PNG, exactly FOUR equal vertical cells in ONE row. Each cell is 512x1024 with a complete tall shrine, frontal view. Exact identical shrine geometry and registration in all four cells. Each shrine has generous 48px horizontal transparent margins and 80px top and bottom margins. No labels, no grid, NO paper backdrop, NO floor shadows.

The shrine is painted with mineral pigment in the style of an early Italian fresco, Giovanni da Modena, not a cartoon, not a 3D render, no polished gold, no neon cyan. A squat carved limestone plinth, its faded vermilion surface bearing a small simple incised circular seal, a dark iron bowl above and a tall wrought-iron ogival shelter. Pale ivory wax drips. Four phases of a small slender PALE SAGE and IVORY flame nestled inside the arch, changing lean left/upright/right/upright; the flame is painted with expressive solid pointed brush shapes, not bloom or VFX glow. Two chains and a piece of mournful red cloth, asymmetrical detail but same silhouette in each frame. Shrine feels handmade, old, protective but ominous. A point of rest amidst judgement, not a fantasy treasure trophy.

Palette warm old ivory limestone, red ochre, slate charcoal iron, restrained ochre rivets, sage flame. Matte painted volume, subtle internal plaster grain, thin brown sinopia outlines that vary naturally, painterly confident broad strokes. Similar to a painted object in a religious mural, not an outline-and-fill illustration. Nothing leaves its cell. Background truly transparent. Output only the four-pose atlas.

Paint four original haunted religious wall fresco scenes as a square 2048x2048 atlas with exactly two columns and two rows, four equal square panels, each an independent matte fresco. Small narrow faded red-ochre edge bands but no bulky frame, no text, no labels. All four share old warm ivory lime plaster, blue-grey charcoal, vermilion, yellow ochre and umber pigments. The background inside each scene is aged warm pale plaster with muted slate space, so it belongs on a pale chapel wall. No black comic outlines, no cartoon facial expressions, no flat vector gradients, no glossy fantasy oil illustration, no 3D rendering. Flesh and drapery have broad painted modelling, delicate sinopia contours and small natural brush marks. Restrained fine lime wear, not thick procedural cracks or a dirty brown overlay.

All human figures wear full, opaque, ankle-length medieval robes. This is ominous symbolic architecture and solemn ritual: no nudity, no injuries, no visible suffering or torture, no blood or violence.
Top left: a towering seated dark animal-headed judge in a heavy robe silently observes a small line of fully clothed pilgrims. The uneasy contrast in scale is inspired by the composition of Giovanni da Modena. A pale gothic arch surrounds the throne. The scene is completely still.
Top right: an orderly diagonal procession of hooded travellers descending broad old stairs toward a distant blue-black doorway. Expressive hands and heavy drapery suggest Michelangelo's compositional rhythm, but there is no fall, collision or torment. A thin red horizon behind.
Bottom left: a silent armoured guardian holds a balance containing two small stones, between two orderly rows of fully clothed adult observers, loosely inspired by Memling's symmetric sacred tableaux. Calm ivory architecture around an unsettling emptiness. No gold shine.
Bottom right: a small boat crossing still black water beneath a distant ancient city at dusk, a tall bird-masked ferryman, fully cloaked adult passengers and an impossible bare tree arch, influenced by Bosch's sense of strange scale. Quiet detailed storytelling, one readable main silhouette, no danger or injury.

All subjects fully painted within their own square and no cross-panel overlap. Make the work feel like four surviving fragments of one painted chapel, not four trading cards. The first image reference provides the intended fresco paint and physical age; use its palette and material rather than copying its FPS composition. Output only this 2x2 atlas.
